questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The average translational kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas depends only on its _____.
questions.explanation: The average translational kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas depends only on its absolute temperature.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The mean-square speed ⟨v²⟩ is the _____ of the squares of the speeds of all the molecules.
questions.explanation: The mean-square speed ⟨v²⟩ is the average of the squares of the speeds of all the molecules.

questions.prompt: Which symbol stands for the x-component of the velocity of molecule 1?
questions.explanation: v_x1 is the x-component of the velocity of molecule 1.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? Neutron stars have overall densities of the order of _____ kg m⁻³.
questions.explanation: Neutron stars have overall densities of the order of 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

questions.prompt: What is the critical temperature of Lanthanum superhydride (LaH₁₀)?
questions.explanation: T_c of Lanthanum superhydride (LaH₁₀) = 250 K.

questions.prompt: In gas equations, what does the symbol P stand for?
questions.explanation: P is the pressure of the gas.

options: The number of molecules per unit volume
The number of moles of the gas

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? Pressure is defined as the force acting per unit _____.
questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as the force acting per unit area.

questions.prompt: Which of these materials has the lowest critical temperature: Aluminium, Tin, Mercury, Lead?
questions.explanation: Aluminium has T_c = 1.18 K, the lowest of the four.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? In terms of the number of molecules N, the ideal gas equation becomes PV = _____.
questions.explanation: In terms of the number of molecules N, the ideal gas equation becomes PV = NkT.

questions.prompt: Which quantity is measured in joule (J)?
questions.explanation: joule (J) is the SI unit of energy.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the force exerted per unit area of a surface?
questions.explanation: Pressure: the force exerted per unit area of a surface.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The root mean square speed is the _____ of the mean-square speed.
questions.explanation: The root mean square speed is the square root of the mean-square speed.

questions.prompt: What does "Boltzmann constant" mean?
questions.explanation: Boltzmann constant: the gas constant per molecule, k = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.

options: the number of molecules in one mole of a substance, 6.022 × 10²³
the constant R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ in the ideal gas equation PV = nRT
the gas constant per molecule, k = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹
the temperature on the kelvin scale, which is directly proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules

questions.prompt: What does "neutron star" mean?
questions.explanation: Neutron star: the remnant of a more massive star in which electrons and protons combine to form neutrons and gravity is balanced by neutron degeneracy pressure.

options: the principle that two electrons cannot occupy the same quantum state
the remnant of a low- to intermediate-mass star in which gravity is balanced by electron degeneracy pressure
the pressure that arises from the Pauli exclusion principle and resists further compression of matter
the remnant of a more massive star in which electrons and protons combine to form neutrons and gravity is balanced by neutron degeneracy pressure

questions.prompt: Which material becomes a superconductor at a critical temperature of 125 K?
questions.explanation: Thallium-based ceramic has T_c = 125 K.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? When a star has used up all of its nuclear fusion fuel, it removes its outer layers and _____ to form a white dwarf.
questions.explanation: When a star has used up all of its nuclear fusion fuel, it removes its outer layers and contracts to form a white dwarf.

questions.prompt: At the same temperature, which gas has the greater rms molecular speed: neon (Ne) or nitrogen (N₂)?
questions.explanation: v_rms = √(3RT/M) is larger for the smaller molar mass: Ne (M = 20 g/mol) is lighter than N₂ (M = 28 g/mol).

options: It depends on the pressure only
Both have the same rms speed

questions.prompt: Which symbol stands for the pressure of the gas?
questions.explanation: P is the pressure of the gas.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? A molecule of mass m with x-velocity v_x1 imparts a momentum of _____ to the wall in one elastic collision.
questions.explanation: A molecule of mass m with x-velocity v_x1 imparts a momentum of \(2mv_{x1}\) to the wall in one elastic collision.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The critical temperature of lead is _____ K.
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of lead is 7.2 K.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The time between two successive collisions of a molecule with the same face of a box of side l is Δt = _____.
questions.explanation: The time between two successive collisions of a molecule with the same face of a box of side l is Δt = \(2l/v_{x1}\).

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? At constant temperature the rms speed of gas molecules is _____ proportional to the square root of the molar mass.
questions.explanation: At constant temperature the rms speed of gas molecules is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass.

questions.prompt: In gas equations, what does the symbol V stand for?
questions.explanation: V is the volume of the gas.

options: The number of molecules of the gas
The Van der Waals constant that corrects for the attraction between molecules
The Van der Waals constant that corrects for the volume of the molecules

questions.prompt: A gas in a rigid container is at 1 atm and 500 K. It is heated to 750 K. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant V and n, P ∝ T: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 1 × 750/500 = 1.50 atm.

questions.prompt: At the same temperature, which gas has the greater rms molecular speed: helium (He) or methane (CH₄)?
questions.explanation: v_rms = √(3RT/M) is larger for the smaller molar mass: He (M = 4 g/mol) is lighter than CH₄ (M = 16 g/mol).

options: It depends on the pressure only
Both have the same rms speed

questions.prompt: A gas in a rigid container is at 2 atm and 250 K. It is heated to 500 K. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant V and n, P ∝ T: P₂ = P₁T₂/T₁ = 2 × 500/250 = 4.00 atm.

questions.prompt: What is the average translational kinetic energy of an ideal gas molecule at 1500 K? (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹)
A gas contains 6.02 × 10²² molecules. How many moles is this? (N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
What does "average speed" mean?
questions.explanation: Average speed: the arithmetic mean of the speeds of the molecules of a gas.

options: the average of the squares of the speeds of all the molecules, written ⟨v²⟩
the arithmetic mean of the speeds of the molecules of a gas
the square root of the mean-square speed of the molecules
the number of molecules per unit volume of a gas, N/V

questions.prompt: Which quantity is measured in cubic metre (m³)?
questions.explanation: cubic metre (m³) is the SI unit of volume.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The rms speed of gas molecules is given by v_rms = _____.
questions.explanation: The rms speed of gas molecules is given by v_rms = \(\sqrt{3kT/m}\).

questions.prompt: Which symbol stands for the number of moles of the gas?
questions.explanation: n is the number of moles of the gas.

questions.prompt: In gas equations, what does the symbol k stand for?
questions.explanation: k is the Boltzmann constant.

options: The mean-square speed of the molecules
The molar mass of the gas

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? The ideal gas law also fails where strong _____ forces act, as in stars.
questions.explanation: The ideal gas law also fails where strong gravitational forces act, as in stars.

questions.prompt: Which symbol stands for the density of the gas?
questions.explanation: ρ is the density of the gas.

questions.prompt: Which term means: the remnant of a low- to intermediate-mass star in which gravity is balanced by electron degeneracy pressure?
questions.explanation: White dwarf: the remnant of a low- to intermediate-mass star in which gravity is balanced by electron degeneracy pressure.

questions.prompt: A gas is at 273 K. What is its temperature on the Celsius scale?
Which option fills the gap correctly? Statistical mechanics connects the _____ details of a system with the macroscopic observables we measure.
questions.explanation: Statistical mechanics connects the microscopic details of a system with the macroscopic observables we measure.

questions.prompt: Which option fills the gap correctly? Increasing the volume of the container makes the collisions of molecules with the walls _____, so the pressure falls.
questions.explanation: Increasing the volume of the container makes the collisions of molecules with the walls less frequent, so the pressure falls.

questions.prompt: Which of these materials has the lowest critical temperature: Aluminium, Tin, Lead, Lanthanum superhydride (LaH₁₀)?
questions.explanation: Aluminium has T_c = 1.18 K, the lowest of the four.

questions.prompt: What does "elastic collision" mean?
questions.explanation: Elastic collision: a collision in which kinetic energy is conserved, so a molecule rebounds from the wall without losing speed.

options: the arithmetic mean of the speeds of the molecules of a gas
the force exerted per unit area of a surface
the average of the squares of the speeds of all the molecules, written ⟨v²⟩
a collision in which kinetic energy is conserved, so a molecule rebounds from the wall without losing speed
